walkthroughs.body_html:
Macbeth (1606) was written for King James I — who believed in the Divine Right of kings.

James also feared witchcraft. Both ideas drive the play's politics and supernatural terror.

The play asks: do the witches cause Macbeth's actions, or does he choose them?

This is the fate vs free will debate — and it has no easy answer.

Macbeth calls his ambition "vaulting" — leaping beyond what's safe.

Lady Macbeth fuels it. Together they commit regicide, and the play tracks the cost.
